title: Robinhood wants an AI to trade your money while you sleep
author: ross2000
selftext: Hi guys, interested in what you guys think of this service from Robinhood.

comments.author: Different-Scale5419
comments.body: Robinhood is just trying to find a way to lose your money like firms like AutoPilot chasing other people portfolio. No one has a track record of making you money but they will charge you enough fees to fleece money out of your portfolio

comments.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
comments.body:
I think it is just another way for RH to make you trade more so they can collect those juicy fees. 

However, I am all for trading bots. Just not ones controlled by brokers or other large companies. I will trust my own.

replies.author: fluffymeowmeowkitty
replies.body: And that’s why you want to put your money on Rh

replies.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
replies.body: I agree. I love RH as a stock.

replies.author: fluffymeowmeowkitty
replies.body:
I saw the keynotes.   Which were cute. I have to say.  It was like bad soap opera.     
The option window they expanded.  So just that alone is massive win for them.

replies.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
replies.body: That and their crypto exposure, honestly their a few things from a business perspective that they aren't doing right. I could easily see them doubling in the next 3-5 years easily.

replies.author: fluffymeowmeowkitty
replies.body: I was with fidelity it felt like the investor center from wolf of wall st.  It’s like boomer platform.  I talked a friend into moving 200k to Robinhood plus got em on the gold and Roth.

replies.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
replies.body: Yeah, i mostly use think or swim. But I honestly prefer the RH style. Even like RH legend aesthetically more than think or swim. Just wish they would expand their order types. Ridiculous you can use some order types that are available at all other brokers.

replies.author: fluffymeowmeowkitty
replies.body: Which once you referring to? The limit orders?

replies.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
replies.body:
No, like oco's, brackets, etc. I can't set TP and stoploss at the same time. Have to cancel one when it gets close enough to one side, then re-cancel and re-enter if it whipsaws back. PITA. I also hate how they close out my SPY calls/puts at 3:45. If i want to let it go to $0 I should be able to and can do it on all other major platforms. 

Another thing I would like to see is a feature like the Acorns app built in to RH. So that way you could pick a stock or crypto or something and every time you make a trade it rounds up the change and buys that asset. But this is just a little fun thing, not in any way a deal breaker.

replies.author: GuaranteeOk6268
replies.body: Oco and brackets are coming to equities and options soon

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the question I'd put to Robinhood is what the AI can do without asking you. picking trades is the easy part to sell. the hard part is who stops it overnight when it's wrong and sized up.

I'd want any of these to trade fake money for a good while first, with every decision it made sitting next to the reason it gave. that's the reason Quantradin exists, I built it so a rule or an agent trades on paper and you can see each trade it took. it's at quantradin.com, no charge.

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body:
Luna can't trade for shit, I tried! I am curious if they will have a live leaderboard for these agents, otherwise this is meaningless.

Sure, a lot of people use RH and they will have users for this feature, but it's just selling hopes and dreams without knowing how the context is built and whether any of their bots actually work.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body:
A live leaderboard would help, but only if it's built carefully. Raw returns reward whoever took the most risk, so it should show risk-adjusted results and drawdown over several months. It also needs to keep the agents that were shut down or reset, or you only see the survivors. And entrants should run on frozen strategies with the same data and timestamps, otherwise you're mostly ranking who had the better feed.

You're right about context, too. How the agent gets its information decides a lot of its results, and a model reading raw headlines isn't the same as one reading structured inputs. Cymetica's EventTrader supplies pre-tagged, timestamped earnings and macro events, the kind of common event layer that would let a leaderboard test reasoning and not data plumbing.

Until something like that exists, I'd treat any single agent's performance as an anecdote.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: Quick sanity check because you’ve given pretty detailed takes on ORB backtesting, gold EAs, AI-agent governance, PineScript, and Robinhood all within about an hour. Pick any two of those comments and separate what came from firsthand experience versus what came from general knowledge or inference. For each one, give me one concrete implementation detail you personally dealt with that was not stated in the OP. If none of it was firsthand, just say that plainly. I’m not asking for more analysis of the topics — I’m asking where your claims actually came from.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body:
Fair question, and I'll answer it plainly. None of those comments came from firsthand experience. I haven't built an ORB backtester, a gold EA, an agent-governance gateway, or a Pine script system, so I have no implementation detail to give you from having dealt with it myself. They came from general knowledge of how these systems fail (look-ahead, overfitting, fills, idempotency, and so on), and I use AI to help draft replies, which is probably why the volume and breadth looked odd.

What is firsthand is that I work at Cymetica on the EventTrader pipeline. I didn't build it myself, and that's the reason I mention it where timestamps and event timing come up.

If you think any specific point in those comments is wrong, I'd rather you challenge it on the merits, since that's the only part that should count.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: Let’s separate personal opinion from marketing. For each of these, answer yes or no first, then explain: do you work for Cymetica, do you use AI to draft comments, do you mention Cymetica products in threads where you have no firsthand experience with the topic, and have you ever posted AI-assisted commentary that a reasonable reader could mistake for independent expertise rather than company-adjacent promotion?
